title: smart-routing fallback incident breadcrumbs - riley scratchpad
content:
Summary:
- Postmortem-in-progress scratchpad for 2024-10-28 regional failover where smart-router did not trigger fallbacks for ~11 minutes for customers in eu-west-1.
- Symptoms: elevated 500/502/504 errors seen from hosted-api ingress, many requests stuck waiting for model variant allocation; smart-routing logs show no fallback decision taken for affected request-ids.

High-level hypothesis (working):
- Race between capacity-check and model-variant mapping update. When eu-west-1 GPUs became overloaded, the routing policy should have picked a fallback (regional fallback to eu-central-1 or model-quantized variant). Instead, we saw decisions that waited for capacity instead of falling back — suggests a stale in-memory routing table or a gating bug in the "prefer-local-unless-unhealthy" policy.

What I observed (raw breadcrumbs):
- 2024-10-28T14:03:12Z request-id=rid_7b2c: client A -> smart-router -> decision: WAIT_FOR_CAPACITY, route attempt to model-v1-eu-west-1.
- 2024-10-28T14:03:45Z request-id=rid_8f1a: client B -> smart-router -> decision: WAIT_FOR_CAPACITY, same.
- 2024-10-28T14:05:31Z many incoming queued tokens, 503 from serving nodes (OOMs), autoscaler triggered.
- 2024-10-28T14:07:01Z logs from region-health-checker: eu-west-1 reported "throttled" with capacity_remaining=0.
- 2024-10-28T14:07:31Z routing-policy reconciler logs: mapping update completed for model-v1 -> allowed_variants [model-v1-quantized-eu, model-v1-eu-central] but reconciler did not flip the policy flag for prefer-local.
- 2024-10-28T14:14:35Z first confirmed fallback routed (eu-central-1) for new requests. Roughly 11 minute gap.

Commands and probes I ran (useful for reproducing and for SRE handoff):
- kubectl -n serving logs --selector=app=smart-router -f --since=30m | grep rid_7b2c
- curl -sS -H 'x-request-id: rid_TEST' -X POST https://internal-router.service/v1/route -d '{"model":"model-v1","region":"eu-west-1","timeout_ms":1000}' -I
- curl -sS https://internal-router.service/v1/status | jq .routes.model-v1
- gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.requestId="rid_7b2c"' --limit 50 --project=redwood-prod
- kubectl exec -it router-xxxx -- sh -c 'ps aux | grep smart-router && cat /etc/router/config.yaml' (to check env flags)

Relevant config / env bits I checked:
- ROUTER_POLICY=prefer-local-unless-unhealthy (set)
- FALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 (default) but smart-router decision path seems to call capacity check with WAIT semantics (no immediate fallback)
- RECONCILE_INTERVAL=30s (reconciler ran at ~14:07:31 and printed mapping update)

Error snippets (copied from logs):
- smart-router stderr: "[ERROR] capacity_check failed: deadline exceeded while waiting for allocation for model-v1-eu-west-1"
- health-checker: "[WARN] region eu-west-1 throttled: active_allocations>limit"
- client-proxy: "upstream prematurely closed connection (server.reset)"
- serving-node: "OOM in TGX worker pid=1223, killing model process"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race/ordering bug: Reconciler updates allowed_variants but policy gating flag (prefer-local toggle) is evaluated earlier and cached; smart-router uses cached policy until restart or TTL expiry -> leads to WAIT rather than fallback.
2) Capacity check call semantics: capacity_check returns WAIT and router waits synchronously for capacity instead of asynchronously offering immediate fallback decision when capacity is below threshold. Config mismatch: FALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS too large or check path mis-coded.
3) KV cache / route cache TTL too long: router looked up a cached mapping that listed eu-west-only variants.
4) Autoscaler slowness combined with fallback penalty: we intentionally bias toward waiting short window to avoid cross-region latency — combined with autoscaler lag caused the break.
5) Authentication/permission edge-case: fallback variants in eu-central were marked as candidate but missing "serving:allowed" tag for some tenants due to a tagging bug in reconcile.

Quick reproduction attempts and notes:
- I force-triggered mapping update locally by POSTing to /admin/reconcile and saw mapping change. However subsequent decision still returned WAIT if the request header X-Prefer-Local=true is present. Suggests per-request header overrides global reconcile in decision flow.
- Running integration test 'routing/decision_fallback_test' reproduces WAIT behavior when capacity_check stub returns WAIT; test expects immediate fallback but code uses 'if capacity==WAIT then sleep up to FALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS then fallback' -> bug in test coverage or changed semantics.

Next steps (short):
- Reproduce in dev: write a harness that stubs capacity_check to return WAIT and assert router returns fallback immediately. Add to CI. (Ethan to pick up test)
- Add additional logging around: (a) which source provided the route mapping (cache vs reconciler), (b) timestamp when mapping last updated, (c) which policy flags were used per-decision. (Olivia)
- Short-term mitigation: reduce FALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS to 250ms for hosted-api tenants in eu regions and enable immediate-fallback flag. (requires rollout and QA)
- Long-term: ensure reconciler pushes atomic policy flip or router subscribes to mapping changes (streaming update). Consider adding versioned mapping and have router check mapping.version on every decision. (engineering follow-up)

Notes for on-call handoff (what to tell SRE):
- Key JIDs: INF-7421 (tracking), slack thread above, PR 1284 has preliminary fix for test and logging.
- If seeing a spike: check smart-router logs for "WAIT_FOR_CAPACITY" vs "FALLBACK_DECIDED" rates, query reconciler logs for mapping version timestamps, and check autoscaler activity in eu-west-1. If mapping.update_ts < 2m and router still returning WAIT, kill one router pod to force reload as emergency rollback (temp).

Questions for the team (open):
- Do we want to prioritize immediate fallback (lower tail-latency) or prefer waiting a short time to keep requests local? Need product guidance on acceptable cross-region fallback.
- Is there a contract for capacity_check return values? Should it ever instruct router to WAIT synchronously? If yes, how long is acceptable?

Random friction / todos in this doc (my brain-dump):
- Add decision telemetry: per-request fields: decision_reason, chosen_variant_origin (cache/reconciler), mapping_version, capacity_snapshot.
- Verify PR 1284 addresses only logging + tests, still need behavior fix (PR notes say "avoid fallback until recon" which might be wrong).
- Follow up with platform-network for cross-region cost impact if we change default policy.

Appendix: quick copy-paste snippets
- curl probe used in debug: curl -v -H "x-request-id: rid_DEBUG" -H "X-Prefer-Local: true" -X POST https://internal-router.service/v1/route -d '{"model":"model-v1","timeout_ms":3000}'
- sample log line: 2024-10-28T14:03:12.345Z [router] rid=rid_7b2c decision=WAIT_FOR_CAPACITY model=model-v1 target_variant=model-v1-eu-west-1 cache_hit=true mapping_version=42

End.

(If anyone reading: add notes here rather than edit the incident doc until we have a consolidated postmortem. This is my working scratchpad.)
